topic: Digital modes: how they work and how to operate them

notes.front: What is WSPR?
notes.back: A digital mode used as a low-power beacon for assessing HF propagation.
notes.explanation: Stations around the world decode each other's very weak WSPR signals to assess which paths are open.
notes.example: Like sending out many quiet test pings and having listeners around the world report back which ones they heard.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is a packet frame's header?
notes.back: The part of the frame that contains routing and handling information.
notes.explanation: Every packet needs to say where it came from and where it is going before the data itself can be delivered.
notes.example: Like the address written on an envelope: the header, not the letter inside, tells the postal system where to send it.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is Baudot code?
notes.back: A 5-bit code with additional start and stop bits, used for RTTY.
notes.explanation: It is the specific digital code named in the rules for RTTY: 'The 5-unit, start-stop, International Telegraph Alphabet No. 2 ... (commonly known as "Baudot")'.
notes.example: Like a five-flag signalling code, bookended by a raise and a lower flag to mark where each letter starts and ends.

notes.front: What does a NAK response mean in an ARQ mode?
notes.back: A request to retransmit the packet.
notes.explanation: The receiving station uses NAK to tell the sender that a packet arrived with errors and must be sent again.
notes.example: Like sending back a smudged form and asking for a clean copy instead of trying to read it.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is forward error correction (FEC)?
notes.back: A technique that lets the receiver correct data errors by sending redundant information along with the data.
notes.explanation: Because the redundancy travels with the original data, the receiver can fix many errors without asking for a retransmission.
notes.example: Like writing a sentence twice in slightly different words, so if one copy is smudged the meaning can still be recovered.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is a time slot in FT8 operation?
notes.back: One of FT8's alternating transmit periods; stations answer in the other slot.
notes.explanation: Good FT8 practice is to answer a CQ in the alternate time slot to the calling station, not on top of it.
notes.example: Like a walkie-talkie conversation where each person waits their turn instead of talking over the other.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is FT4?
notes.back: A weak-signal digital mode, like FT8, sent on USB when using AFSK.
notes.explanation: It belongs to the same family of weak-signal digital modes as FT8, sharing the same sideband convention.
notes.example: Like FT8, FT4 is sent on USB when AFSK is used.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is JT65?
notes.back: A weak-signal digital mode, like FT8, sent using AFSK on the standard sideband USB.
notes.explanation: Like FT8 and FT4, JT65 is sent on USB when using AFSK.
notes.example: Like an earlier version of the FT8 idea: slower, but built for the same very weak signals.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is JT9?
notes.back: A weak-signal digital mode, like FT8 and JT65, sent on USB when using AFSK.
notes.explanation: It is one more member of the same family of narrow, weak-signal AFSK modes tested together on the exam.
notes.example: Like a sibling mode to JT65 and FT8, built for the same job of copying very weak signals.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is PSK31?
notes.back: A keyboard-to-keyboard digital mode whose upper-case letters use longer Varicode bit sequences and so slow transmission.
notes.explanation: PSK31 is popular for live typed conversation on HF.
notes.example: Like a typewriter where capital letters simply take a little longer to strike than lower-case ones.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is Varicode?
notes.back: The variable-length code used to send characters in a PSK31 signal.
notes.explanation: Common lower-case letters get short codes and rarer characters like upper-case letters get longer ones, which keeps average transmission fast.
notes.example: Like Morse code giving common letters short sequences: Varicode applies the same idea to PSK31.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is AREDN?
notes.back: An Amateur Radio Emergency Data Network: a mesh network providing high-speed data during an emergency or community event.
notes.explanation: Its microwave nodes re-route data automatically if one node fails, which is why it suits emergency and event use.
notes.example: Like a group of relay runners who can each take a different route if one path is blocked, so the message still gets through.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What are mark and space?
notes.back: The names for the two separate frequencies of a frequency shift keyed (FSK) signal.
notes.explanation: If a receiver has the two swapped, or is on the wrong sideband, an otherwise correctly tuned FSK signal will not decode.
notes.example: Like two colours of light used to signal 'on' and 'off' instead of a single flashing light.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is a waterfall display?
notes.back: A display where frequency is horizontal, signal strength is shown as intensity, and time runs vertically.
notes.explanation: As time passes, older data scrolls down the screen like water falling, giving the display its name.
notes.example: Like a scrolling weather radar image, but for radio signals across a band of frequencies over time.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is D-STAR?
notes.back: One of the digital voice modes amateurs use, alongside DMR and System Fusion.
notes.explanation: It is one of the three digital voice systems the pool names together.
notes.example: Like one of several competing but related digital phone standards, similar in purpose to DMR and System Fusion.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is System Fusion?
notes.back: One of the digital voice modes amateurs use, alongside DMR and D-STAR.
notes.explanation: One of the three digital voice systems the pool names with DMR and D-STAR.
notes.example: Like a third brand of digital phone standard alongside DMR and D-STAR, serving the same purpose.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is RTTY?
notes.back: Narrow-band direct-printing telegraphy: a digital mode sent using a specifically authorised digital code.
notes.explanation: The rules list RTTY as its own emission type, separate from phone, CW or data emissions.
notes.example: Like an automated typewriter link: each transmitted character is printed directly at the far end.

notes.front: What is AFSK?
notes.back: Audio frequency shift keying: sending an FSK-coded digital mode as an audio tone through an SSB transmitter.
notes.explanation: AFSK is how many digital modes, including RTTY and FT8, are carried over an ordinary SSB radio rather than a dedicated FSK transmitter.
notes.example: Like whistling two different notes into a normal telephone to send a two-state signal, instead of needing a special line.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is a baud?
notes.back: A unit of signalling rate: symbols sent per second.
notes.explanation: Choosing the wrong baud rate is one of three faults (with reversed mark/space and wrong sideband) that can silently defeat RTTY decoding.
notes.example: Like two typists agreeing on a typing speed beforehand: if one types faster than the other expects, the message comes out garbled.

notes.front: What is PACTOR?
notes.back: A digital protocol, used for example with Winlink, whose connections are limited to two stations.
notes.explanation: Unlike a net, a PACTOR link is strictly point-to-point: a third station cannot join an existing connection.
notes.example: Like a private phone call: exactly two parties, and no one else can dial in and join.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is VARA?
notes.back: A digital protocol used with Winlink.
notes.explanation: It is one of the protocols, alongside PACTOR, that a Winlink station can use to move email-style messages over radio.
notes.example: Like one of two different courier services that can carry the same Winlink mail.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is a Winlink Remote Message Server (RMS)?
notes.back: Another name for a Winlink gateway station.
notes.explanation: It is the station that bridges a radio link to the internet-based Winlink email system.
notes.example: Like a post office branch that hands mail between a local courier route and the national postal network.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What digital mode is used as a low-power beacon for assessing HF propagation?
notes.back: WSPR.
notes.explanation: Its whole purpose is propagation reporting, unlike conversational modes such as PSK31 or FT8.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What part of a packet radio frame contains the routing and handling information?
notes.back: The header.
notes.explanation: Routing information has to come before the data itself so intermediate stations know where to forward the packet.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: How is Baudot code structured?
notes.back: A 5-bit code with additional start and stop bits.
notes.explanation: The start and stop bits mark where each character begins and ends.

notes.front: What happens after too many failed retransmission attempts in an ARQ mode?
notes.back: The connection is dropped.
notes.explanation: ARQ keeps retrying on a NAK, but gives up and disconnects rather than retrying forever.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: How does forward error correction let a receiver correct data errors?
notes.back: By transmitting redundant information along with the data.
notes.explanation: That redundancy is what lets the receiver reconstruct correct data without asking the sender to repeat anything.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What three things does good FT8 practice need: clock accuracy, which slot to answer in, and which sideband?
notes.back: Computer time accurate to about 1 second; answer in the alternate time slot; use USB.
notes.explanation: FT8's tight timing and slot structure depend on all operators sharing the same accurate clock and sideband convention.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: Where in the 20 m band is FT8 commonly found, and what does an FT8 report of +3 mean?
notes.back: About 14.074 to 14.077 MHz; a signal-to-noise ratio equivalent to +3 dB in a 2.5 kHz bandwidth.
notes.explanation: FT8's report scale is normalised to a standard bandwidth so operators can compare signal quality consistently.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What code does PSK31 use to send characters, and why do upper-case letters slow transmission?
notes.back: Varicode; upper-case letters use longer Varicode bit sequences.
notes.explanation: Shorter codes for common characters keep average PSK31 throughput high, at the cost of longer codes for less common ones.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What happens to a packet on a mesh network if one node fails, and what is AREDN's primary purpose?
notes.back: It may still reach its target via an alternate node; AREDN provides high-speed data during an emergency or community event.
notes.explanation: Automatic re-routing is what makes a mesh network resilient compared with a single fixed path.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: How are the two separate frequencies of an FSK signal identified?
notes.back: As mark and space.
notes.explanation: Getting these swapped, or listening on the wrong sideband, is a common reason an apparently well-tuned FSK signal fails to decode.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What does a waterfall display show, and what do vertical lines beside a signal indicate?
notes.back: Frequency horizontal, strength as intensity, time vertical; vertical lines indicate overmodulation.
notes.explanation: Splatter from an overmodulated signal spreads energy into adjacent frequencies, which appears as extra vertical streaks on the waterfall.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What three systems provide digital voice modes for amateurs?
notes.back: DMR, D-STAR, and System Fusion.
notes.explanation: These are the three digital voice systems the pool names together as a complete set.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What sideband and shift are normal for RTTY via AFSK on an SSB transmitter, and what three faults can stop it decoding?
notes.back: LSB; 170 Hz shift; reversed mark/space, wrong baud rate, or wrong sideband.
notes.explanation: All three faults can occur even when a signal looks properly tuned, which is why RTTY troubleshooting checks each in turn.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What describes Winlink, and how do you contact a Winlink gateway station?
notes.back: An amateur email network over radio, a form of packet radio, working on VHF and HF; transmit a connect message on its published frequency.
notes.explanation: Winlink combines several familiar ideas (email, packet radio, VHF/HF operation) into one system, reached the same way as any published station.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: Which mode is normally used when sending RTTY signals via AFSK with an SSB transmitter?
notes.back: LSB
notes.choices:
A) USB
B) DSB
C) CW
D) LSB
notes.choicesExplained: A: USB is the convention for FT8/JT65/JT9/FT4, not RTTY. B: DSB is not a sideband selection used for AFSK RTTY on an SSB rig. C: CW is on-off keyed Morse, not RTTY.
notes.explanation: By accepted amateur practice, AFSK RTTY on SSB is sent on LSB, the opposite convention from the newer AFSK data modes.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E01

notes.front: What is VARA?
notes.back: A digital protocol used with Winlink
notes.choices:
A) A low signal-to-noise digital mode used for EME (moonbounce)
B) A digital protocol used with Winlink
C) A radio direction finding system used on VHF and UHF
D) A DX spotting system using a network of software defined radios
notes.choicesExplained: A: EME weak-signal modes are things like JT65, not VARA. C: VARA is not a direction-finding system. D: VARA is not a DX spotting network.
notes.explanation: VARA is one of the protocols a Winlink station can use to move data reliably over a radio link.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E02

notes.front: What symptoms may result from other signals interfering with a PACTOR or VARA transmission?
notes.back: All these choices are correct
notes.choices:
A) Frequent retries or timeouts
B) Long pauses in message transmission
C) Failure to establish a connection between stations
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C are each individually true but incomplete; the pool keys the combined answer.
notes.explanation: Interference disrupts the ARQ exchange these protocols rely on, which can show up as retries, pauses or a failed connection.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E03

notes.front: Which of the following is good practice when choosing a transmitting frequency to answer a station calling CQ using FT8?
notes.back: Find a clear frequency during the alternate time slot to the calling station
notes.choices:
A) Always call on the station’s frequency
B) Call on any frequency in the waterfall except the station’s frequency
C) Find a clear frequency during the same time slot as the calling station
D) Find a clear frequency during the alternate time slot to the calling station
notes.choicesExplained: A: calling on the same frequency and slot causes a collision. B: any frequency without regard to the time slot still risks a collision in the same slot. C: replying in the same time slot as the CQ collides with it.
notes.explanation: FT8's time-slot structure is designed so replies go out in the slot when the calling station is listening, not transmitting.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E04

notes.front: What is the standard sideband for JT65, JT9, FT4, or FT8 digital signal when using AFSK?
notes.back: USB
notes.choices:
A) LSB
B) USB
C) DSB
D) SSB
notes.choicesExplained: A: LSB is the RTTY convention, the opposite of these modes. C: DSB is not the sideband selection used for these modes. D: "SSB" alone does not specify upper or lower.
notes.explanation: These newer AFSK digital modes standardise on USB, unlike traditional AFSK RTTY, which uses LSB.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E05

notes.front: What is the most common frequency shift for RTTY emissions in the amateur HF bands?
notes.back: 170 Hz
notes.choices:
A) 85 Hz
B) 170 Hz
C) 425 Hz
D) 850 Hz
notes.choicesExplained: A: 85 Hz is narrower than the common HF RTTY shift. C, D: these are wider shifts than the common amateur HF convention.
notes.explanation: 170 Hz between mark and space is the widely used amateur HF RTTY shift.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E06

notes.front: Which of the following is required when using FT8?
notes.back: Computer time accurate to within approximately 1 second
notes.choices:
A) A special hardware modem
B) Computer time accurate to within approximately 1 second
C) Receiver attenuator set to -12 dB
D) A vertically polarized antenna
notes.choicesExplained: A: the pool keys only accurate time as required. C: no fixed attenuator setting is required. D: no particular antenna polarisation is required.
notes.explanation: FT8's tight time-slot structure only works if every station's clock is closely synchronised.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E07

notes.front: In what segment of the 20-meter band are most digital mode operations commonly found?
notes.back: Between 14.070 MHz and 14.100 MHz
notes.choices:
A) At the bottom of the slow-scan TV segment, near 14.230 MHz
B) At the top of the SSB phone segment, near 14.325 MHz
C) In the middle of the CW segment, near 14.100 MHz
D) Between 14.070 MHz and 14.100 MHz
notes.choicesExplained: A: 14.230 MHz is the slow-scan TV area, not general digital activity. B: 14.325 MHz is in the phone segment. C: 14.100 MHz is a beacon frequency, not the centre of digital activity.
notes.explanation: This range is the voluntary band-plan home for most 20 m digital activity, distinct from phone and beacon segments.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E08

notes.front: How do you join a contact between two stations using the PACTOR protocol?
notes.back: Joining an existing contact is not possible, PACTOR connections are limited to two stations
notes.choices:
A) Send broadcast packets containing your call sign while in MONITOR mode
B) Transmit a steady carrier until the PACTOR protocol times out and disconnects
C) Joining an existing contact is not possible, PACTOR connections are limited to two stations
D) Send a NAK code
notes.choicesExplained: A: broadcasting your call sign does not add you to an existing PACTOR link. B: forcing a timeout does not let you join, it only ends the other stations' link. D: sending a NAK is part of error correction within a link, not a way to join one.
notes.explanation: PACTOR is strictly point-to-point, so a third station can never join a contact already in progress.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E09

notes.front: Which of the following is a way to establish contact with a digital messaging system gateway station?
notes.back: Transmit a connect message on the station’s published frequency
notes.choices:
A) Send an email to the system control operator
B) Send QRL in Morse code
C) Respond when the station broadcasts its SSID
D) Transmit a connect message on the station’s published frequency
notes.choicesExplained: A: email cannot itself establish a radio link. B: QRL asks if a frequency is busy, it does not connect to a gateway. C: a gateway does not broadcast an SSID to be answered.
notes.explanation: A gateway listens on its published frequency for an incoming connect request, just like any published digital station.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E10

notes.front: What is the primary purpose of an Amateur Radio Emergency Data Network (AREDN) mesh network?
notes.back: To provide high-speed data services during an emergency or community event
notes.choices:
A) To provide FM repeater coverage in remote areas
B) To provide real time propagation data by monitoring amateur radio transmissions worldwide
C) To provide high-speed data services during an emergency or community event
D) To provide DX spotting reports to aid contesters and DXers
notes.choicesExplained: A: AREDN is a data mesh network, not an FM repeater system. B: it does not exist to monitor propagation. D: it is not a DX spotting service.
notes.explanation: AREDN's mesh nodes are built to deliver high-bandwidth data exactly when normal infrastructure may be unavailable.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E11

notes.front: Which of the following describes Winlink?
notes.back: All these choices are correct
notes.choices:
A) An amateur radio wireless network to send and receive email on the internet
B) A form of Packet Radio
C) A wireless network capable of both VHF and HF band operation
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C are each individually true but incomplete; the pool keys the combined answer.
notes.explanation: Winlink combines email delivery, a packet-radio foundation, and operation on both VHF and HF into one system.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E12

notes.front: What is another name for a Winlink Remote Message Server?
notes.back: Gateway
notes.choices:
A) Terminal Node Controller
B) Gateway
C) RJ-45
D) Printer/Server
notes.choicesExplained: A: a Terminal Node Controller is separate packet-radio hardware, not the RMS itself. C: RJ-45 is a physical network connector, not a Winlink role. D: "Printer/Server" is not the correct term.
notes.explanation: The Remote Message Server bridges the radio link to the internet-based Winlink system, exactly what a gateway does.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E13

notes.front: What could be wrong if you cannot decode an RTTY or other FSK signal even though it is apparently tuned in properly?
notes.back: All these choices are correct
notes.choices:
A) The mark and space frequencies may be reversed
B) You may have selected the wrong baud rate
C) You may be listening on the wrong sideband
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C are each individually true but incomplete; the pool keys the combined answer.
notes.explanation: Any of these three faults can leave a signal looking correctly tuned on screen while still failing to decode.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E14

notes.front: Which of the following is a common location for FT8?
notes.back: Approximately 14.074 MHz to 14.077 MHz
notes.choices:
A) Anywhere in the voice portion of the band
B) Anywhere in the CW portion of the band
C) Approximately 14.074 MHz to 14.077 MHz
D) Approximately 14.110 MHz to 14.113 MHz
notes.choicesExplained: A, B: FT8 has its own narrow band-plan spot, not the whole voice or CW segment. D: that range is not the standard FT8 location.
notes.explanation: This narrow slice of the 20 m band is the voluntary band-plan home for FT8 activity.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G2E15

notes.front: Which digital mode is used as a low-power beacon for assessing HF propagation?
notes.back: WSPR
notes.choices:
A) WSPR
B) MFSK16
C) PSK31
D) SSB-SC
notes.choicesExplained: B: MFSK16 is a keyboard mode, not a propagation beacon. C: PSK31 is for live conversation, not propagation testing. D: SSB-SC (suppressed carrier) is a general phone technique, not a beacon mode.
notes.explanation: WSPR was built specifically to test propagation with very weak, automatically decoded beacon transmissions.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C02

notes.front: What part of a packet radio frame contains the routing and handling information?
notes.back: Header
notes.choices:
A) Directory
B) Preamble
C) Header
D) Trailer
notes.choicesExplained: A: a packet frame has no "directory" section. B: a preamble is a synchronisation pattern, not routing data. D: a trailer typically holds error-checking information, not routing.
notes.explanation: The header sits at the front of the frame so routing decisions can be made before the rest of the data is even read.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C03

notes.front: Which of the following describes Baudot code?
notes.back: A 5-bit code with additional start and stop bits
notes.choices:
A) A 7-bit code with start, stop, and parity bits
B) A code using error detection and correction
C) A 5-bit code with additional start and stop bits
D) A code using SELCAL and LISTEN
notes.choicesExplained: A: 7-bit with parity describes a different, later code, not Baudot. B: Baudot itself provides no error detection or correction. D: SELCAL and LISTEN are not part of Baudot.
notes.explanation: Baudot's 5 data bits plus start and stop bits is exactly the structure the rules describe for this code.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C04

notes.front: In an ARQ mode, what is meant by a NAK response to a transmitted packet?
notes.back: Request retransmission of the packet
notes.choices:
A) Request retransmission of the packet
B) Packet was received without error
C) Receiving station connected and ready for transmissions
D) Entire file received correctly
notes.choicesExplained: B, D: these describe a successful, error-free receipt, the opposite of what NAK signals. C: readiness to receive is a separate connection-status signal, not a NAK.
notes.explanation: NAK is the receiver's way of telling the sender that the packet must be sent again.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C05

notes.front: What action results from a failure to exchange information due to excessive transmission attempts when using an ARQ mode?
notes.back: The connection is dropped
notes.choices:
A) The checksum overflows
B) The connection is dropped
C) Packets will be routed incorrectly
D) Encoding reverts to the default character set
notes.choicesExplained: A: a checksum does not "overflow" as a defined failure mode here. C: misrouting is not the described consequence. D: encoding does not revert to a default character set.
notes.explanation: ARQ gives up and disconnects rather than retrying an unreachable link indefinitely.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C06

notes.front: Which of the following narrow-band digital modes can receive signals with very low signal-to-noise ratios?
notes.back: FT8
notes.choices:
A) MSK144
B) FT8
C) AMTOR
D) MFSK32
notes.choicesExplained: A, C, D: the pool keys FT8 as the mode built for very low SNR.
notes.explanation: FT8's coding is specifically designed to pull decodable data out of signals well below the noise floor.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C07

notes.front: Which of the following statements is true about PSK31?
notes.back: Upper case letters use longer Varicode bit sequences and thus slow down transmission
notes.choices:
A) Upper case letters are sent with more power
B) Upper case letters use longer Varicode bit sequences and thus slow down transmission
C) Error correction is used to ensure accurate message reception
D) Higher power is needed as compared to RTTY for similar error rates
notes.choicesExplained: A: PSK31 does not vary transmit power by letter case. C: PSK31 has no built-in error correction. D: PSK31 typically needs less, not more, power than RTTY for similar reliability.
notes.explanation: Varicode assigns shorter codes to common characters, so the rarer upper-case letters take longer to send.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C08

notes.front: Which is true of mesh network microwave nodes?
notes.back: If one node fails, a packet may still reach its target station via an alternate node
notes.choices:
A) Having more nodes increases signal strengths
B) If one node fails, a packet may still reach its target station via an alternate node
C) Links between two nodes in a network may have different frequencies and bandwidths
D) More nodes reduce overall microwave out of band interference
notes.choicesExplained: A: more nodes do not by themselves increase signal strength. C: not the keyed choice; the pool tests re-routing around a failed node (B). D: more nodes do not, by themselves, reduce out-of-band interference.
notes.explanation: Automatic re-routing around a failed node is the defining resilience feature of a mesh network.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C09

notes.front: How does forward error correction (FEC) allow the receiver to correct data errors?
notes.back: By transmitting redundant information with the data
notes.choices:
A) By controlling transmitter output power for optimum signal strength
B) By using the Varicode character set
C) By transmitting redundant information with the data
D) By using a parity bit with each character
notes.choicesExplained: A: FEC is not about power control. B: Varicode is a specific character code for PSK31, not the mechanism of FEC in general. D: a single parity bit alone only detects, it does not correct, errors.
notes.explanation: The redundant information sent alongside the data is what lets the receiver reconstruct correct values without a retransmission.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C10

notes.front: How are the two separate frequencies of a Frequency Shift Keyed (FSK) signal identified?
notes.back: Mark and space
notes.choices:
A) Dot and dash
B) On and off
C) High and low
D) Mark and space
notes.choicesExplained: A: dot and dash describe Morse code elements, not FSK's two frequencies. B: FSK signals are always present, not switched on and off. C: "high and low" is not the standard FSK terminology.
notes.explanation: Mark and space are the standard names for FSK's two discrete transmitted frequencies.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C11

notes.front: Which type of code is used for sending characters in a PSK31 signal?
notes.back: Varicode
notes.choices:
A) Varicode
B) Viterbi
C) Volumetric
D) Binary
notes.choicesExplained: B: Viterbi is a decoding algorithm used elsewhere, not PSK31's character code. C: "Volumetric" is not a real code name. D: "Binary" alone is too generic; PSK31 specifically uses the variable-length Varicode.
notes.explanation: Varicode's variable-length scheme is specifically what makes PSK31 efficient for typed text.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C12

notes.front: What is indicated on a waterfall display by one or more vertical lines on either side of a data mode or RTTY signal?
notes.back: Overmodulation
notes.choices:
A) Long path propagation
B) Backscatter propagation
C) Insufficient modulation
D) Overmodulation
notes.choicesExplained: A, B: propagation modes are not shown by vertical splatter lines on a waterfall. C: insufficient modulation would not create extra splatter; it is the opposite problem.
notes.explanation: The splatter from overmodulation spreads energy to nearby frequencies, appearing as vertical streaks beside the main signal.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C13

notes.front: Which of the following describes a waterfall display?
notes.back: Frequency is horizontal, signal strength is intensity, time is vertical
notes.choices:
A) Frequency is horizontal, signal strength is vertical, time is intensity
B) Frequency is vertical, signal strength is intensity, time is horizontal
C) Frequency is horizontal, signal strength is intensity, time is vertical
D) Frequency is vertical, signal strength is horizontal, time is intensity
notes.choicesExplained: A, B, D: these swap which axis carries frequency, strength and time; only C matches the standard waterfall layout.
notes.explanation: This layout lets an operator watch how activity across a whole band changes over time, at a glance.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C14

notes.front: What does an FT8 signal report of +3 mean?
notes.back: The signal-to-noise ratio is equivalent to +3dB in a 2.5 kHz bandwidth
notes.choices:
A) The signal is 3 times the noise level of an equivalent SSB signal
B) The signal is S3 (weak signals)
C) The signal-to-noise ratio is equivalent to +3dB in a 2.5 kHz bandwidth
D) The signal is 3 dB over S9
notes.choicesExplained: A: FT8 reports are an SNR figure, not a simple multiple of noise level. B, D: FT8's report scale is not the same as an S meter reading.
notes.explanation: FT8 normalises its SNR report to a standard 2.5 kHz bandwidth so reports are comparable between stations.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C15

notes.front: Which of the following provide digital voice modes?
notes.back: DMR, D-STAR, and SystemFusion
notes.choices:
A) WSPR, MFSK16, and EasyPAL
B) FT8, FT4, and FST4
C) Winlink, PACTOR II, and PACTOR III
D) DMR, D-STAR, and SystemFusion
notes.choicesExplained: A: WSPR, MFSK16 and EasyPAL are data or image modes, not voice. B: FT8, FT4 and FST4 are weak-signal data modes, not voice. C: Winlink and PACTOR are messaging systems, not voice modes.
notes.explanation: DMR, D-STAR and System Fusion (spelt "SystemFusion" in the pool) are the three named digital voice systems the pool groups together.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G8C16

notes.front: What is the difference between the sideband convention for AFSK RTTY and for FT8/JT65/JT9/FT4?
notes.back: AFSK RTTY on SSB is sent on LSB; FT8, JT65, JT9 and FT4 use USB.
notes.explanation: Being on the wrong sideband is one of the classic reasons a digital signal fails to decode, so this pairing is tested directly.
notes.contrast: RTTY: LSB, 170 Hz shift, mark and space. FT8 and family: USB, narrower tones, strict time slots.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is the difference between Varicode and Baudot code?
notes.back: Varicode is a variable-length code used by PSK31; Baudot is a fixed 5-bit code, plus start and stop bits, used by RTTY.
notes.explanation: Varicode's variable length lets common characters go faster; Baudot's fixed length keeps every character the same size.
notes.contrast: Varicode (PSK31): variable length, shorter for common letters. Baudot (RTTY): fixed 5 bits plus start/stop bits.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)

notes.front: What is the difference between ARQ and forward error correction (FEC)?
notes.back: ARQ asks the sender to retransmit a bad packet (using a NAK); FEC sends redundant information so the receiver can correct errors without a retransmission.
notes.explanation: ARQ needs a return channel to request retries; FEC works even one-way, without needing a reply from the receiver.
notes.contrast: ARQ: two-way, retransmission on NAK. FEC: works one-way, corrects using built-in redundancy.
notes.source: 2023-2027 General Class Pool and Syllabus, 6th Errata (4 Feb 2026)
